question: You have an application that will run on Compute Engine. You must design an architecture that accounts for a disaster recovery plan requiring the application to fail over to another region if a regional outage occurs. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the application on two Compute Engine instances in the same project but in a different region. Use the first instance to serve traffic, and use an external Application Load Balancer to fail over to the standby instance in case of a disaster.
options.B: Deploy the application on a Compute Engine instance. Use the instance to serve traffic, and use an external Application Load Balancer to fail over to an instance on your premises in case of a disaster.
options.C: Deploy the application on two Compute Engine instance groups, each in the same project but in a different region. Use the first instance group to serve traffic, and use an external Application Load Balancer to fail over to the standby instance group in case of a disaster.
options.D: Deploy the application on two Compute Engine instance groups, each in a separate project and a different region. Use the first instance group to serve traffic, and use an external Application Load Balancer to fail over to the standby instance group in case of a disaster.

explanation: A global external Application Load Balancer can distribute traffic across backend instance groups in multiple regions and automatically direct traffic to a healthy region when the primary region becomes unavailable. Using one Compute Engine instance group per region provides independent, scalable application backends for regional disaster recovery. The backend groups should be in the same project for the standard configuration.

question:
You have a Compute Engine application that should autoscale when total memory utilization exceeds 80%. You installed the Ops Agent and configured the autoscaling policy as follows:

Metric identifier: agent.googleapis.com/memory/percent_used

Filter: metric.label.state = 'used'

Target utilization level: 80

Target type: GAUGE

The application does not scale during high load. You want to fix this. What should you do?

options.A: Change the Target type to DELTA_PER_MINUTE.
options.B: Change the Metric identifier to agent.googleapis.com/memory/bytes_used.
options.C: Change the filter to metric.label.state = 'used' AND metric.label.state = 'buffered' AND metric.label.state = 'cached' AND metric.label.state = 'slab'.
options.D: Change the filter to metric.label.state = 'free' and the Target utilization to 20.

explanation: The agent.googleapis.com/memory/percent_used metric is broken out by state (used, buffered, cached, slab, free) whose values sum to 100%. On Linux much RAM is reported as buffered/cached, so the strictly 'used' state can stay well below 80% even under heavy load, meaning a filter of state='used' with target 80 never triggers scaling. Filtering state='free' with a target of 20 correctly scales out when free memory drops below 20% (equivalent to total utilization exceeding 80%). Option C is invalid because a single metric label cannot equal several values simultaneously (the AND filter matches nothing), and DELTA_PER_MINUTE (A) is wrong for a gauge metric.

question:
You have a Compute Engine managed instance group that adds and removes Compute Engine instances in response to your application's load. The instances use a shutdown script to remove REDIS database entries associated with each instance. You notice that many database entries were not removed and suspect the shutdown script is the cause.

You must ensure the commands in the shutdown script execute reliably whenever an instance is shut down. You create a Cloud Run function to remove the database entries. What should you do next?

options.A: Modify the shutdown script to wait for 30 seconds before triggering the Cloud Run function.
options.B: Do not use the Cloud Run function. Modify the shutdown script to restart if it has not completed in 30 seconds.
options.C: Set up a Cloud Logging sink that triggers the Cloud Run function after an instance removal log message arrives in Cloud Logging.
options.D: Modify the shutdown script to wait for 30 seconds and then publish a message to a Pub/Sub queue.

explanation: Compute Engine executes shutdown scripts on a best-effort basis, and a script can be forcibly stopped before it completes. Triggering the cleanup from an instance-removal log event moves the work outside the terminating VM, so the Cloud Run function can remove the associated Redis entries independently of shutdown-script completion. Cloud Logging sinks can route matching log entries to a destination for event-driven processing.

question: You run a cluster on Kubernetes Engine (GKE) that serves a web application. Users report that a particular part of the application no longer responds. You observe that every pod in your deployment restarts after 2 seconds. The application writes logs to standard output. You need to inspect the logs to determine the cause of the issue. Which approach can you use?

options.A: Review the Cloud Logging logs for each Compute Engine instance that is serving as a node in the cluster.
options.B: Review the Cloud Logging logs for the specific GKE container that is serving the unresponsive part of the application.
options.C: Connect to the cluster using gcloud credentials and connect to a container in one of the pods to read the logs.
options.D: Review the Serial Port logs for each Compute Engine instance that is serving as a node in the cluster.

explanation: GKE automatically collects workload logs written to standard output and standard error and makes them available in Cloud Logging as k8s_container logs. Reviewing the logs for the specific application container is therefore the appropriate way to diagnose an application component whose pods are repeatedly restarting.

question: You need to ensure application and operational reliability by enabling dependable task scheduling for compute on GCP. Following Google best practices, what should you do?

options.A: Using the Cron service provided by App Engine, publish messages directly to a message-processing utility service running on Compute Engine instances.
options.B: Using the Cron service provided by App Engine, publish messages to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic. Subscribe to that topic using a message-processing utility service running on Compute Engine instances.
options.C: Using the Cron service provided by Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), publish messages directly to a message-processing utility service running on Compute Engine instances.
options.D: Using the Cron service provided by GKE, publish messages to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic. Subscribe to that topic using a message-processing utility service running on Compute Engine instances.

explanation: The reliable scheduling pattern for Compute Engine uses App Engine Cron Service for scheduling and Cloud Pub/Sub for asynchronous, fault-tolerant messaging. A message-processing utility running on Compute Engine subscribes to the Pub/Sub topic, allowing scheduled work to be delivered independently of individual VM availability and supporting controlled distribution to workers.

question: Refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. KnightMotives wants to personalize its dealer experience for customers and has chosen to train its own AI models for personalized recommendations. The company will begin collecting personally identifiable information (PII) from customers for use as training data for the models. KnightMotives wants to ensure maximum security and worldwide compliance. You must ensure that the data is encrypted both at rest and while AI model training occurs, without affecting model accuracy. What should you do?

options.A: Store the training data in BigQuery using column-level encryption. Train the model using Confidential GKE Nodes.
options.B: Store the training data in BigQuery using column-level encryption Train the model on Agent Platform Workbench instances using customer-managed encryption keys.
options.C: Process all data with Sensitive Data Protection’s de-identification service. Replace any PII with a random string before storing it. Train the model using Confidential GKE Nodes.
options.D: Process all data with Sensitive Data Protection's de-identification service. Replace any PII with a random string before storing it. Train the model on Agent Platform Workbench instances using customer-managed encryption keys.

explanation: BigQuery column-level encryption protects PII at rest, while Confidential GKE Nodes use hardware-backed memory encryption to protect data in use during model training without requiring application changes that could affect model accuracy. Replacing PII with random strings can remove or distort useful personalization signals, and customer-managed encryption keys on Agent Platform Workbench protect resources at rest rather than data being processed in memory.

question:
Refer to the Helicopter Racing League (HRL) case study. Your team is responsible for creating a payment-card data vault for card numbers used to bill tens of thousands of viewers, merchandise consumers, and season ticket holders. You must implement a custom card-tokenization service that meets these requirements:

It must deliver low latency at minimal cost.

It must identify duplicate credit cards and must not retain plaintext card numbers.

It should support annual key rotation.

Which storage approach should you use for the tokenization service?

options.A: Store the card data in Secret Manager after running a query to identify duplicates.
options.B: Encrypt the card data with a deterministic algorithm stored in Firestore using Datastore mode.
options.C: Encrypt the card data with a deterministic algorithm and shard it across multiple Memorystore instances.
options.D: Use column-level encryption to store the data in Cloud SQL.

explanation: Deterministic encryption yields the same ciphertext or token for each occurrence of the same card number, preserving referential integrity so duplicates can be identified without storing plaintext. Firestore in Datastore mode provides managed, scalable document storage with pay-per-use pricing, while Cloud KMS can maintain a scheduled annual rotation for the encryption key. Google Cloud Sensitive Data Protection documents deterministic AES-SIV encryption as preserving referential integrity for tokenization use cases.

question: You need to migrate Hadoop jobs for your company’s Data Science team without changing the underlying infrastructure. You want to minimize costs and the effort required to manage infrastructure. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Managed Service for Apache Spark cluster using standard worker instances.
options.B: Create a Managed Service for Apache Spark cluster using Spot VM worker instances.
options.C: Manually deploy a Hadoop cluster on Compute Engine using standard instances.
options.D: Manually deploy a Hadoop cluster on Compute Engine using Spot VM instances.

explanation: Managed Service for Apache Spark (formerly Dataproc) is a fully managed Hadoop and Spark service that creates and manages clusters and job orchestration, avoiding the administration required by a manually deployed Compute Engine Hadoop cluster. Spot VM workers lower compute cost for fault-tolerant batch workloads, making a Managed Service for Apache Spark cluster with Spot VM workers the best fit.

question:
Mountkirk Games wants to establish a continuous-delivery pipeline. Its architecture contains many small services that it needs to update and roll back quickly. Mountkirk Games has these requirements:

Services are deployed redundantly across multiple regions in the US and Europe.

Only frontend services are exposed on the public internet.

They can provide a single frontend IP for their fleet of services.

Deployment artifacts are immutable.

Which product set should they use?

options.A: Google Cloud Storage, Google Cloud Dataflow, Google Compute Engine
options.B: Google Cloud Storage, Google App Engine, Google Network Load Balancer
options.C: Google Kubernetes Registry, Google Container Engine, Google HTTP(S) Load Balancer
options.D: Google Cloud Functions, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, Google Cloud Deployment Manager

explanation: A container registry provides versioned container deployment artifacts, and Google Kubernetes Engine (formerly Google Container Engine) supports deploying and rolling back independently managed services. A global external HTTP(S) load balancer provides a single public entry point and can route internet traffic to healthy service backends across multiple regions, allowing only frontend services to be publicly exposed. Immutable container image tags or digests ensure a deployed artifact cannot be silently replaced.

question:

KnightMotives is a car manufacturer that specializes in autonomous, self-driving vehicles, including Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), hybrids, and traditional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles. Although KnightMotives has advanced the in-vehicle experience in its BEV fleet, the hybrid and ICE vehicles have not yet adopted these new systems and are regarded poorly by critics and drivers. The absence of modern in-vehicle technology in hybrid and ICE vehicles has led to declining sales and customer satisfaction.

KnightMotives wants to modernize the consumer experience across all vehicles within five years. Artificial Intelligence provides a unique opportunity to transform the in-vehicle experience, as well as the shopping, buying, and service/maintenance experience. Investing in this new technology will require a global shift in financial priorities.

KnightMotives also wants to enhance its unreliable online ordering system. Systems that let customers build their vehicle online for acquisition through a dealer are not providing the data or reliability dealers require, causing a strain in the relationship between KnightMotives and dealers. Service technicians and sales staff require improved tooling to advance dealer success, including for built-to-order vehicles.

Solution Concept —

KnightMotives wants to move from manufacturing cars to creating a complete and compelling “automotive experience.” The strategy emphasizes delivering a consistent experience across all models, developing AI-powered features, producing new revenue through data monetization, adopting a digital focus to distinguish its brand from competitors, and creating better tools for mechanics and salespeople.

Existing Technical Environment —

KnightMotives's IT is primarily on-premises, with some applications on major cloud platforms. Its supply chain operates on an outdated mainframe, and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) is also outdated, making new promotions and dealer discounts hard to implement. Dealers have no budget for new equipment. Vehicles are fragmented across multiple code bases, with significant technical debt caused by supporting backward compatibility. Network connectivity to manufacturing plants and vehicle connectivity in rural areas are challenges.

Business Requirements —

Key business requirements include cultivating a personalized relationship with the driver and providing a cohesive experience across all models. Establishing a better build-to-order model will reduce time on the lot and offer transparency to both dealers and customers. KnightMotives also seeks to monetize corporate data to fund new technology investments, because its current AI infrastructure is obsolete and corporate data is still siloed. Security is a primary concern because of previous data breaches. Compliance with European Union (EU) data-protection regulations, especially for emerging autonomous platforms, is critical.

KnightMotives plans significant investments in fully autonomous-driving capabilities, with initial implementation aimed at regions with favorable regulatory environments. Employee upskilling, attracting top-tier talent, and improving communication between business and technical teams are also critical goals.

Technical Requirements —

Modernizing the in-vehicle experience includes creating a consistent user experience (UX) that seamlessly integrates AI-powered features across all models, updating in-vehicle hardware and software in legacy models to support new UX features and AI capabilities, and ensuring dependable network connectivity—especially in rural areas—to support real-time AI features and data transmission.

Network upgrades are required to support greater data traffic and improve connectivity between plants and headquarters.

IT infrastructure modernization requires adopting a hybrid-cloud strategy to gain the benefits of both on-premises and cloud infrastructure, and progressively modernizing or replacing legacy systems to increase efficiency and agility.

Autonomous-vehicle development and testing requires investing in leading AI and machine-learning technologies, building a robust simulation environment, and ensuring compliance with evolving autonomous-vehicle regulations.

Data monetization and insights requires implementing a robust data-management platform, strict data-security and privacy measures, and scalable AI/ML infrastructure.

Increased emphasis on security and risk management involves implementing a comprehensive security framework to protect against cyber threats and data breaches, developing an incident-response plan, and providing security-awareness training to employees.

Delivering a delightful experience for dealers and customers requires improving the online build-to-order system; developing modern dealer tools to streamline dealer operations, including sales, service, and inventory management; and implementing a comprehensive Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system to track customer interactions, personalize experiences, and improve customer satisfaction.

Executive Statement —

KnightMotives is committed to improving safety and saving lives by using an extensive body of data—including driving, road conditions, behavioral studies, and crash-safety statistics—to create compelling digital experiences for drivers. Our AI consistently exceeds national safety statistics, ensuring that the distinctive and coveted KnightMotives experience is aligned across all vehicle models.

Michael Knight, KnightMotives CEO

For this question, use the KnightMotives Automotive case study. You are responsible for designing the network infrastructure architecture for KnightMotives's new Google Cloud environment. You need to design the new VPC topology. You want to provide guaranteed bandwidth and low latency between the plants and Google Cloud resources. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Standard Tier VPC. and ensure a subnet is available in the region closest to a plant. Establish a Cloud Interconnect between each subnet and the local plant.
options.B: Create a Standard Tier VPC. and ensure a subnet is available in the region closest to a plant Establish Direct Peering between Google's Edge Network and the local plant.
options.C: Create a Premium Ter VPand ensure a subnet is available in the region closest to a plant. Establish a Cloud Interconnect between each subnet and the local plant.
options.D: Create a Premium Ter VPC. and ensure a subnet is available in the region closest to a plant. Establish Direct Peering between Google's Edge Network and the local plant.

explanation: Cloud Interconnect provides dedicated connectivity between on-premises networks and VPC networks, avoiding the public internet and supporting scalable connection capacity, low latency, and high availability. Premium Tier is intended to optimize network performance. Direct Peering is not the appropriate mechanism for private connectivity from plants to VPC resources.

question: You developed an application with Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform that identifies famous paintings from uploaded images. You need to test the application and let specific people upload images during the next 24 hours. Not every user has a Google Account. How should users upload images?

options.A: Have users upload the images to Cloud Storage. Protect the bucket with a password that expires after 24 hours.
options.B: Have users upload the images to Cloud Storage using a signed URL that expires after 24 hours.
options.C: Create an App Engine web application where users can upload images. Configure App Engine to disable the application after 24 hours. Authenticate users via Cloud Identity.
options.D: Create an App Engine web application where users can upload images for the next 24 hours. Authenticate users via Cloud Identity.

explanation: A Cloud Storage signed URL can grant time-limited permission to upload a particular object. Anyone who has the signed URL can use it without a Google Account, and its expiration can be set to 24 hours.

question: The operations team at your company wants to retain Cloud VPN log events for one year. You need to configure the cloud infrastructure to store these logs. What should you do?

options.A: Set up a filter in Cloud Logging and a Cloud Storage bucket as an export target for the logs you want to save.
options.B: Enable the Compute Engine API, and then enable logging on the firewall rules that match the traffic you want to save.
options.C: Set up a Cloud Logging Dashboard titled Cloud VPN Logs, and then add a chart that queries for the VPN metrics over a one-year time period.
options.D: Set up a filter in Cloud Logging and a topic in Pub/Sub to publish the logs.

explanation: A Cloud Logging sink can apply an inclusion filter for the required Cloud VPN log entries and route matching entries to a Cloud Storage bucket. Cloud Storage is a supported Cloud Logging sink destination for long-term log storage; configure the bucket so that no lifecycle policy removes the archived objects before one year.

question: For this question, refer to the EHR Healthcare case study. EHR Healthcare recently suffered unauthorized access to its Kubernetes-based applications because credentials were compromised, resulting in a security breach. You must secure access between its on-premises systems and the Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) environment, while preserving regulatory compliance and integrating with EHR's existing identity provider. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider in GKE, and integrate it with Active Directory for centralized authentication and fine-grained authorization controls.
options.B: Establish a secure VPN tunnel between the on-premises network and the GKE VPC, and implement strict firewall rules to restrict access based on source IP addresses and ports.
options.C: Configure Workload Identity Federation with Active Directory to enable authentication and authorization for applications across both Kubernetes environments.
options.D: Create a service account with minimal permissions for each application running in GKE, and distribute the credentials securely to the on-premises systems.

explanation: An OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider integrated with Active Directory centralizes authentication through the existing enterprise identity system and can pass user and group claims for fine-grained Kubernetes RBAC authorization. This reduces reliance on separately distributed long-lived credentials and supports auditable, policy-based access controls required for regulated environments. GKE supports external identity providers that use OIDC, with identity claims mapped to Kubernetes users and groups for authorization.

question: You need to deploy Microsoft SQL Server on GCP. Management requires no downtime if a data center outage occurs in any zone within a GCP region. What should you do?

options.A: Configure a Cloud SQL instance with high availability enabled.
options.B: Configure a Cloud Spanner instance with a regional instance configuration.
options.C: Set up SQL Server on Compute Engine, using Always On Availability Groups using Windows Failover Clustering. Place nodes in different subnets.
options.D: Set up SQL Server Always On Availability Groups using Windows Failover Clustering. Place nodes in different zones.

explanation: SQL Server Always On Availability Groups use Windows Server Failover Clustering to provide automatic high availability. Placing cluster nodes in different zones within the same region isolates replicas from a zonal data-center outage, allowing a surviving replica to take over. Google Cloud documents a deployment with SQL Server cluster nodes distributed across different zones for this purpose.

question:
Your company uses the Firewall Insights feature in Google Network Intelligence Center and has several firewall rules applied to Compute Engine instances.

You need to assess the efficiency of the applied firewall ruleset. When you open the Firewall Insights page in the Google Cloud Console, you find that no log rows are displayed. What should you do to troubleshoot this issue?

options.A: Enable Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) flow logging.
options.B: Enable Firewall Rules Logging for the firewall rules you want to monitor.
options.C: Verify that your user account is assigned the compute.networkAdmin Identity and Access Management (IAM) role.
options.D: Install the Google Cloud SDK, and verify that there are no Firewall logs in the command line output.

explanation: Firewall Insights metrics and log-based usage insights are generated from Firewall Rules Logging and are available only for firewall rules that have Firewall Rules Logging enabled. Enable that logging on the firewall rules being monitored so Firewall Insights can collect and display their usage data.

question:
You want to automate creation of a managed instance group. The VMs have many OS package dependencies, and you want to minimize startup time for new VMs in the instance group.

What should you do?

options.A: Use Terraform to create the managed instance group and a startup script to install the OS package dependencies.
options.B: Create a custom VM image with all OS package dependencies. Use Infrastructure Manager to create the managed instance group with the VM image.
options.C: Use Puppet to create the managed instance group and install the OS package dependencies.
options.D: Use Infrastructure Manager to create the managed instance group and Ansible to install the OS package dependencies.

explanation: A custom VM image preinstalls the required OS package dependencies, so each new VM does not need to download and install them during boot. Google Cloud documents that custom images are more deterministic and start more quickly than VMs configured with startup scripts, and that image baking provides a shorter time from boot to application readiness.

question:
For this question, use the Mountkirk Games case study. You are responsible for the architecture of the new Game Backend Platform. The game communicates with the backend through a REST API.

You want to follow Google-recommended practices. How should you design the backend?

options.A: Create an instance template for the backend. For every region, deploy it on a multi-zone managed instance group. Use an L4 load balancer.
options.B: Create an instance template for the backend. For every region, deploy it on a single-zone managed instance group. Use an L4 load balancer.
options.C: Create an instance template for the backend. For every region, deploy it on a multi-zone managed instance group. Use an L7 load balancer.
options.D: Create an instance template for the backend. For every region, deploy it on a single-zone managed instance group. Use an L7 load balancer.

explanation: Application Load Balancers provide Layer 7 load balancing for HTTP and HTTPS traffic, which is appropriate for a REST API. A regional managed instance group spreads identical VM instances across multiple zones, protecting the backend from a zonal failure and supporting a highly available serving workload.

question:
The database administration team has asked for your help improving the performance of its new database server running on Google Compute Engine. The database imports and normalizes its performance statistics and is built with MySQL running on Debian Linux. They have an n1-standard-8 virtual machine with 80 GB of SSD persistent disk.

What should they change to obtain better performance from this system?

options.A: Increase the virtual machine's memory to 64 GB
options.B: Create a new virtual machine running PostgreSQL
options.C: Dynamically resize the SSD persistent disk to 500 GB
options.D: Migrate their performance metrics warehouse to BigQuery
options.E: Modify all of their batch jobs to use bulk inserts into the database

explanation: SSD Persistent Disk performance scales with disk size, up to the performance limits of the attached VM. Resizing the 80 GB SSD Persistent Disk to 500 GB increases the disk’s available IOPS and throughput, improving the database’s storage-intensive import and normalization operations.

question:
The marketing department plans to send a promotional email campaign. The development team wants to minimize direct operations management. They anticipate customer response ranging from 100 to 500,000 click-throughs per day. The link directs users to a simple website that explains the promotion and gathers user information and preferences.

Which infrastructure should you recommend?

options.A: Use Google App Engine to serve the website and Firestore in Datastore mode to store user data.
options.B: Use a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster to serve the website and store data to persistent disk.
options.C: Use a managed instance group to serve the website and Google Cloud Bigtable to store user data.
options.D: Use a single Compute Engine virtual machine (VM) to host a web server, backend by Google Cloud SQL.

explanation: Google App Engine is a managed application platform that automatically scales application instances in response to traffic volume. Firestore in Datastore mode is a fully managed, automatically scalable NoSQL database suited to storing user-submitted information and preferences. Together, they accommodate highly variable demand with minimal operational management.

question:
Dress4Win has asked you to recommend the machine types on which they should deploy their application servers.

How should you proceed?

options.A: Perform a mapping of the on-premises physical hardware cores and RAM to the nearest machine types in the cloud.
options.B: Recommend that Dress4Win deploy application servers to machine types that offer the highest RAM to CPU ratio available.
options.C: Recommend that Dress4Win deploy into production with the smallest instances available, monitor them over time, and scale the machine type up until the desired performance is reached.
options.D: Identify the number of virtual cores and RAM associated with the application server virtual machines align them to a custom machine type in the cloud, monitor performance, and scale the machine types up until the desired performance is reached.

explanation: Virtual CPU and memory allocations from the existing application-server VMs provide a practical baseline for an initial cloud configuration. Compute Engine custom machine types allow CPU and memory to be specified independently within the selected machine family’s limits, and observed workload performance should drive subsequent resizing.

question:
The company wants to experiment with the cloud while keeping risk low. It wants to archive approximately 100 TB of log data in the cloud, test the analytics capabilities available there, and retain the data as a long-term disaster-recovery backup.

Which two actions should you take?

options.A: Load logs into Google BigQuery
options.B: Load logs into Google Cloud SQL
options.C: Import logs into Google Cloud Observability
options.D: Insert logs into Google Cloud Bigtable
options.E: Upload log files into Google Cloud Storage

explanation: BigQuery supports loading and querying large-scale data for analytics. Cloud Storage provides highly durable storage and its Archive class is designed for long-term archiving, online backup, and disaster recovery, so keeping the log files there preserves a durable backup while BigQuery enables analysis.

question:
An application sends HTTP requests to Cloud Storage. From time to time, those requests fail with 5xx and 429 HTTP status codes.

How should these error types be handled?

options.A: Use gRPC instead of HTTP for better performance.
options.B: Implement retry logic using a truncated exponential backoff strategy.
options.C: Make sure the Cloud Storage bucket is multi-regional for geo-redundancy.
options.D: Monitor https://status.cloud.google.com/feed.atom and only make requests if Cloud Storage is not reporting an incident.

explanation: Cloud Storage treats HTTP 429 and 5xx responses as transient errors that can be retried. A truncated exponential backoff strategy increases the delay between attempts up to a limit, reducing repeated load during rate limiting or temporary service failures. Retries should be limited and applied only to operations that are safe to retry.

question: Your company is designing its application landscape on Compute Engine. When a zonal outage occurs, the application must be restored in another zone as quickly as possible with the most recent application data. You need to design a solution that meets this requirement. What should you do?

options.A: Create a snapshot schedule for the disk containing the application data. Whenever a zonal outage occurs, use the latest snapshot to restore the disk in the same zone.
options.B: Configure the Compute Engine instances with an instance template for the application, and use a regional persistent disk for the application data. Whenever a zonal outage occurs, use the instance template to spin up the application in another zone in the same region. Use the regional persistent disk for the application data.
options.C: Create a snapshot schedule for the disk containing the application data. Whenever a zonal outage occurs, use the latest snapshot to restore the disk in another zone within the same region.
options.D: Configure the Compute Engine instances with an instance template for the application, and use a regional persistent disk for the application data. Whenever a zonal outage occurs, use the instance template to spin up the application in another region. Use the regional persistent disk for the application data.

explanation: Regional Persistent Disk synchronously replicates disk data between two zones in the same region, providing the current data and enabling failover after a zonal outage. An instance template supports quickly creating the replacement Compute Engine instance in the healthy zone. Snapshot-based recovery can lose changes made after the last snapshot and adds restoration time; regional disks are not a cross-region failover mechanism.

question:
JencoMart wants to migrate its User Profiles database to Google Cloud Platform.

Which Google Database should it use?

options.A: Cloud Spanner
options.B: Google BigQuery
options.C: Google Cloud SQL
options.D: Google Cloud Datastore

explanation: Cloud Datastore is a fully managed, scalable NoSQL document database for application data. Google Cloud documentation specifically identifies user profiles that provide customized experiences based on past activities and preferences as a suitable Datastore use case.

question:
Your company needs to track whether a person is present in a meeting room reserved for a scheduled meeting. There are 1,000 meeting rooms across 5 offices on 3 continents. Each room has a motion sensor that reports its status every second. Motion-detector data contains only a sensor ID and several different discrete pieces of information. Analysts will use this data along with information about account owners and office locations.

Which database type should you use?

options.A: Flat file
options.B: NoSQL
options.C: Relational
options.D: Blobstore

explanation: High-volume sensor telemetry with 1,000 devices reporting every second requires horizontal scalability and flexible schema. NoSQL databases excel at this workload, efficiently storing keyed records with discrete status attributes while supporting ad-hoc queries against reference data (account owners, locations). Relational databases impose overhead on high-velocity writes; flat files and blobstores are not queryable.

question: Mountkirk Games needs to secure connectivity from its new gaming application platform to Google Cloud. You want to simplify the process while following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.A: Configure Workload Identity and service accounts to be used by the application platform.
options.B: Use Kubernetes Secrets, which are obfuscated by default. Configure these Secrets to be used by the application platform.
options.C: Configure Kubernetes Secrets to store the secret, enable Application-Layer Secrets Encryption, and use Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS) to manage the encryption keys. Configure these Secrets to be used by the application platform.
options.D: Configure HashiCorp Vault on Compute Engine, and use customer managed encryption keys and Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS) to manage the encryption keys. Configure these Secrets to be used by the application platform.

explanation: Workload Identity Federation for GKE lets Kubernetes workloads authenticate to Google Cloud through Kubernetes and IAM service accounts, using short-lived credentials and fine-grained IAM permissions. It avoids storing and managing service-account keys in Kubernetes Secrets, making it the recommended, streamlined authentication method for GKE workloads accessing Google Cloud services.

question:
A customer operates a web service that e-commerce sites use to provide product recommendations to users. The company has started experimenting with a machine learning model on Google Cloud Platform to improve result quality.

What should the customer do to improve the model’s results over time?

options.A: Export Agent Platform performance metrics from Cloud Monitoring to BigQuery, to be used to analyze the efficiency of the model.
options.B: Build a roadmap to move the machine learning model training from Cloud GPUs to Cloud TPUs, which offer better results.
options.C: Monitor Compute Engine announcements for availability of newer CPU architectures, and deploy the model to them as soon as they are available for additional performance.
options.D: Save a history of recommendations and results of the recommendations in BigQuery, to be used as training data.

explanation: A recommendation model improves when it is retrained with historical recommendations and their observed outcomes, such as clicks, purchases, or other feedback. BigQuery can retain this growing interaction dataset for analysis and model training, enabling the model to learn which recommendations were effective.

question: A company is developing a new application that will let globally distributed users upload pictures and share them with selected users. The application must support millions of concurrent users. The company wants developers to focus only on writing code, without creating or maintaining the underlying infrastructure. Which service should be used to deploy the application?

options.A: App Engine
options.B: Cloud Endpoints
options.C: Compute Engine
options.D: Google Kubernetes Engine

explanation: App Engine is a fully managed, serverless platform for hosting web applications at scale. It provisions servers and automatically scales application instances as demand changes, allowing developers to concentrate on application code rather than infrastructure management.

question: Your team is building a web application that will be deployed on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Your CTO expects a successful launch, and you must ensure that the application can support the anticipated load of tens of thousands of users. You want to test the current deployment to confirm that application latency remains below a specified threshold. What should you do?

options.A: Use a load testing tool to simulate the expected number of concurrent users and total requests to your application, and inspect the results.
options.B: Enable autoscaling on the GKE cluster and enable horizontal pod autoscaling on your application deployments. Send curl requests to your application, and validate if the auto scaling works.
options.C: Replicate the application over multiple GKE clusters in every Google Cloud region. Configure a global external Application Load Balancer to expose the different clusters over a single global IP address.
options.D: Use Cloud Debugger in the development environment to understand the latency between the different microservices.

explanation: Load testing simulates the expected number of concurrent users and request volume, allowing latency and other performance results to be measured against the required threshold. Google Cloud guidance states that controlled load testing helps assess capacity-planning trade-offs such as throughput and latency.

question:
Your development team has built a structured API for retrieving vehicle data. They want third parties to develop dealership tools that use this vehicle event data. You want to enable delegated authorization for this data.

What should you do?

options.A: Build or leverage an OAuth-compatible access control system
options.B: Build SAML 2.0 SSO compatibility into your authentication system
options.C: Restrict data access based on the source IP address of the partner systems
options.D: Create secondary credentials for each dealer that can be given to the trusted third party

explanation: OAuth-compatible access control supports delegated authorization: a resource owner can authorize a third-party client to access protected API resources through scoped, time-limited, and revocable access tokens without disclosing the resource owner’s credentials.

question: You have an application running on Google Kubernetes Engine in a Deployment named echo-deployment. The Deployment is exposed through a Service named echo-service. You need to update the application while minimizing application downtime. What should you do?

options.A: Use kubectl set image deployment/echo-deployment <new-image>
options.B: Use the rolling update functionality of the Instance Group behind the Kubernetes cluster
options.C: Update the deployment yaml file with the new container image. Use kubectl delete deployment/echo-deployment and kubectl create ג€"f <yaml-file>
options.D: Update the service yaml file which the new container image. Use kubectl delete service/echo-service and kubectl create ג€"f <yaml-file>

explanation: Changing the container image of an existing Kubernetes Deployment initiates a Deployment rollout. The rolling-update mechanism replaces Pods progressively while retaining available Pods to serve traffic through the Service, minimizing application downtime.

question:
You are designing a new insurance claims-processing application that will be deployed on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). Your company’s compliance team requires a complete, non-repudiable audit trail for every administrative action from day one. The application must record:

Who deploys a new container image

Who changes the GKE cluster’s configuration

Who uses kubectl to interact with running pods or Kubernetes secrets

What should you do?

options.A: Enable Binary Authorization on the GKE cluster, and create a policy that requires all deployed container images to be signed by a trusted attestor.
options.B: Deploy a DaemonSet to every node in the GKE cluster that runs a logging agent to collect and forward all container logs to Cloud Logging.
options.C: Enable GKE Audit Logging to send Kubernetes API server logs to Cloud Logging, and ensure Cloud Audit Logs are enabled for the project.
options.D: Activate the Security Command Center Premium tier to analyze GKE logs and detect threats, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations in real time.

explanation: GKE audit logs are generated by the Kubernetes API server and record Kubernetes API actions, including changes made with kubectl to resources such as Pods, Deployments, and Secrets. Cloud Audit Logs records administrative and access activity for Google Cloud resources, including GKE cluster operations. Admin Activity logs capture configuration writes, while Data Access logs must be explicitly enabled when needed for read/write access coverage. Sending these audit records to Cloud Logging provides the centralized record of caller, action, target resource, and time needed for the audit trail.

question: A customer support application stores every email and chat conversation in Cloud Bigtable for retention and analysis. What is the recommended way to sanitize personally identifiable information or payment card information in this data before its initial storage?

options.A: Hash all data using SHA256
options.B: Encrypt all data using elliptic curve cryptography
options.C: De-identify the data with Sensitive Data Protection
options.D: Use regular expressions to find and redact phone numbers, email addresses, and credit card numbers

explanation: Google Cloud Sensitive Data Protection can inspect text for sensitive data, including personally identifiable information and payment-card data, and de-identify detected values through transformations such as masking, removal, tokenization, or encryption. This provides purpose-built detection and sanitization before persistent storage, unlike broad hashing/encryption or limited regular-expression matching.

question:
For this question, refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. KnightMotives has built and deployed a Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform model that provides personalized recommendations in the new car-configuration application. Customers receive optional-equipment recommendations best suited to their persona. The model-training features were derived from previous usage data from the car-configuration application.

From prior experience, you know that customer behavior can change over time. For example, during periods of economic certainty and rising stock markets, customers tend to buy more expensive options. You want to detect when customer behavior changes gradually over time so that you can adjust the model. What should you do?

options.A: Configure Model Monitoring, and select training-serving skew detection.
options.B: Configure Model Monitoring, and select prediction drift detection.
options.C: Configure Knowledge Catalog auto data quality on the prediction request data features using row-level rules.
options.D: Configure Knowledge Catalog auto data quality on the prediction request data features using aggregate rules.

explanation: Prediction drift detection in Model Monitoring on Agent Platform identifies significant changes over time in production prediction data, allowing changes in customer behavior and recommendation patterns to be detected so the model can be adjusted. Training-serving skew detection compares production data with the training-data baseline rather than specifically monitoring temporal drift.

question: You need to deploy an application on Google Cloud that must run in a Debian Linux environment. The application needs extensive configuration to function correctly. You want to ensure that Debian distribution updates can be installed with minimal manual intervention as they become available. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Compute Engine instance template using the most recent Debian image. Create an instance from this template, and install and configure the application as part of the startup script. Repeat this process whenever a new Google-managed Debian image becomes available.
options.B: Create a Debian-based Compute Engine instance, install and configure the application, and use OS patch management to install available updates.
options.C: Create an instance with the latest available Debian image. Connect to the instance via SSH, and install and configure the application on the instance. Repeat this process whenever a new Google-managed Debian image becomes available.
options.D: Create a Docker container with Debian as the base image. Install and configure the application as part of the Docker image creation process. Host the container on Google Kubernetes Engine and restart the container whenever a new update is available.

explanation: Google Cloud VM Manager Patch automates operating-system and software patch updates for Compute Engine VMs through scheduled patch deployments. For Debian systems, it supports distribution updates, so an already configured Debian VM can remain in place while available updates are applied with minimal manual effort.

question: An organization uses Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) to manage a complex Kubernetes environment across multiple cloud providers. You need to deploy a solution that streamlines configuration management, enforces security policies, and ensures consistent application deployment throughout all environments. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.A: Leverage Argo CD for GitOps-based continuous delivery and Open Policy Agent (OPA) for policy enforcement, and develop a controller for multi-cluster configuration management.
options.B: Deploy Crossplane for managing cloud resources as Kubernetes objects, FluxCD for GitOps-based configuration synchronization, and Kyverno for policy enforcement.
options.C: Deploy Kustomize for configuration customization, Config Sync with multiple Git repositories, and a script to enforce security policies.
options.D: Utilize Config Sync as part of GKE to synchronize configurations from a centralized repository, and utilize Policy Controller to enforce policies using OPA Gatekeeper.

explanation: Config Sync synchronizes Kubernetes configurations from a centralized source of truth across a fleet of clusters, helping prevent configuration drift and consistently deploy configurations, policies, and workloads. Policy Controller is Google’s integrated policy engine, based on OPA Gatekeeper, for enforcing programmable security, compliance, and best-practice guardrails across clusters. Google documents this combination for enforcing common configuration across infrastructure, including GKE on AWS.

question:
Operational settings, such as oil pressure, can be adjusted on each of TerramEarth's vehicles to improve efficiency according to environmental conditions. Your primary objective is to improve the operating efficiency of all 20 million cellular and unconnected vehicles in the field.

How can you achieve this objective?

options.A: Have you engineers inspect the data for patterns, and then create an algorithm with rules that make operational adjustments automatically
options.B: Capture all operating data, train machine learning models that identify ideal operations, and run locally to make operational adjustments automatically
options.C: Implement a Google Cloud Dataflow streaming job with a sliding window, and use Google Cloud Messaging (GCM) to make operational adjustments automatically
options.D: Capture all operating data, train machine learning models that identify ideal operations, and host in Google Cloud Machine Learning (ML) Platform to make operational adjustments automatically

explanation: Models trained on operating data can learn the relationship between environmental conditions and efficient vehicle settings. Running inference locally enables automatic adjustments with low latency and continues to function when a vehicle has no network connection; cloud-hosted inference or cloud messaging cannot reliably serve unconnected vehicles.

question:
You are deploying an application to Google Cloud. The application is part of a system. The application in Google Cloud must communicate over a private network with applications in a non-Google Cloud environment. The anticipated average throughput is 200 kbps. The business requires:

availability of the system as close to 100% as possible

cost optimization

You need to design connectivity between the locations that meets the business requirements. What should you provision?

options.A: An HA Cloud VPN gateway connected with two tunnels to an on-premises VPN gateway
options.B: Two Classic Cloud VPN gateways connected to two on-premises VPN gateways Configure each Classic Cloud VPN gateway to have two tunnels, each connected to different on-premises VPN gateways
options.C: Two HA Cloud VPN gateways connected to two on-premises VPN gateways Configure each HA Cloud VPN gateway to have two tunnels, each connected to different on-premises VPN gateways
options.D: A single Cloud VPN gateway connected to an on-premises VPN gateway

explanation: An HA Cloud VPN gateway configured with two tunnels—one to each of two separate on-premises VPN gateways—provides the 99.99% HA VPN availability SLA. It uses the minimum redundant HA VPN topology needed for the low-throughput connection; additional HA gateways and tunnels increase cost without being required for this topology. Classic VPN offers a lower availability SLA.

question:
During a high-traffic period of the day, one of your relational databases crashes, but its replica is never promoted to primary. You want to prevent this from happening again.

What should you do?

options.A: Use a different database
options.B: Choose larger instances for your database
options.C: Create snapshots of your database more regularly
options.D: Implement routinely scheduled failovers of your databases

explanation: Regularly scheduled failovers test whether the standby can be promoted and whether clients reconnect correctly during a failure. Cloud SQL recommends testing failover to observe an application’s response to automatic failover; backups and larger instances do not validate the promotion path.

question: You need to implement network ingress for a new game that satisfies the established business and technical requirements. Mountkirk Games wants every regional game instance to be deployed in multiple Google Cloud regions. What should you do?

options.A: Configure a global load balancer connected to a managed instance group running Compute Engine instances.
options.B: Configure kubemci with a global load balancer and Google Kubernetes Engine.
options.C: Configure a global load balancer with Google Kubernetes Engine.
options.D: Configure Ingress for Anthos with a global load balancer and Google Kubernetes Engine.

explanation: kubemci is deprecated and its repository archived. The supported way to expose workloads running in GKE clusters across multiple regions behind a single global external load balancer is Multi Cluster Ingress (formerly Ingress for Anthos), which provisions one anycast VIP and routes users to the closest healthy cluster.

question:
A developer on your team deployed an application to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) using the Dockerfile below. They report that application deployments take too long.

You need to optimize this Dockerfile for faster deployment times without adversely affecting the application's functionality. Which two actions should you take?

options.A: Remove Python after running pip
options.B: Remove dependencies from requirements.txt
options.C: Use a slimmed-down base image like Alpine Linux
options.D: Use larger machine types for your Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) node pools
options.E: Copy the source after he package dependencies (Python and pip) are installed

explanation: Using a slim, compatible base image such as Alpine Linux can substantially reduce container image size and therefore reduce image-pull and deployment time. Installing the runtime packages before copying application source lets Docker cache those layers, so ordinary source-code changes do not require reinstalling Python and pip.

question: Your organization is cloud-native and makes extensive use of Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) to run containerized workloads. You want to adopt infrastructure as code (IaC) principles to simplify and automate the provisioning, configuration, and management of Google Cloud resources while minimizing operational cost. What should you do?

options.A: Install Config Sync, and use YAML manifests in your GitHub repository to automate the provisioning and management of Google Cloud resources.
options.B: Install Config Connector, and use Python to define the desired state of your Google Cloud resources. Apply the Python scripts to provision and manage the resources.
options.C: Set up Config Controller, and use YAML manifests to define the desired state of your Google Cloud resources. Apply these YAML configurations to provision and manage the resources.
options.D: Develop a custom Kubernetes operator within your GKE cluster to automate the execution of your IaC scripts for provisioning and managing Google Cloud resources.

explanation: Config Controller provides a managed environment for using YAML manifests to declare the desired state of Google Cloud resources. It uses Config Connector, whose Kubernetes custom resources and controllers create, manage, and reconcile Google Cloud resources to that desired state, avoiding the operational burden of building and maintaining a custom solution. Config Connector overview

question: Refer to the Mountkirk Games case study for this question. Mountkirk Games wants to future-proof its solution so it can benefit from cloud and technology improvements as they become available. Which two actions should it take?

options.A: Store as much analytics and game activity data as financially feasible today so it can be used to train machine learning models to predict user behavior in the future.
options.B: Begin packaging their game backend artifacts in container images and running them on Google Kubernetes Engine to improve the ability to scale up or down based on game activity.
options.C: Set up a CI/CD pipeline using Jenkins and Spinnaker to automate canary deployments and improve development velocity.
options.D: Adopt a schema versioning tool to reduce downtime when adding new game features that require storing additional player data in the database.
options.E: Implement a weekly rolling maintenance process for the Linux virtual machines so they can apply critical kernel patches and package updates and reduce the risk of 0-day vulnerabilities.

explanation: Future-proofing means positioning to exploit future cloud and technology improvements. Storing as much analytics and game-activity data as is financially feasible now (A) preserves raw signal that can later train machine-learning models to predict user behavior once those capabilities are adopted. Packaging the game backend as container images on Google Kubernetes Engine (B) gives portable, elastically scalable workloads that readily absorb new platform features and scale with game activity. C (a fixed Jenkins/Spinnaker toolchain) and E (weekly manual VM patching) are point implementation choices that lock in specific tooling and legacy VM operations rather than future-proofing, and D (schema versioning) addresses deployment downtime, not benefiting from future cloud improvements.

question: You manage several Google Cloud projects and must interact daily with BigQuery, Bigtable, and Kubernetes Engine by using the gcloud CLI tool. You travel frequently and use different workstations during the week. You want to avoid managing the gcloud CLI manually. What should you do?

options.A: Use Google Cloud Shell in the Google Cloud Console to interact with Google Cloud.
options.B: Create a Compute Engine instance and install gcloud on the instance. Connect to this instance via SSH to always use the same gcloud installation when interacting with Google Cloud.
options.C: Install gcloud on all of your workstations. Run the command gcloud components auto-update on each workstation
options.D: Use a package manager to install gcloud on your workstations instead of installing it manually.

explanation: Google Cloud Shell provides browser-based command-line access with the Google Cloud CLI preinstalled, authenticated with the user’s Google credentials, and kept up to date. It can be used from different workstations without maintaining separate local gcloud installations.

question:
Your application must process credit card transactions. You want to minimize the scope of Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance without reducing the ability to analyze transactional data and trends related to the payment methods used.

How should you design the architecture?

options.A: Create a tokenizer service and store only tokenized data
options.B: Create separate projects that only process credit card data
options.C: Create separate subnetworks and isolate the components that process credit card data
options.D: Streamline the audit discovery phase by labeling all of the virtual machines (VMs) that process PCI data
options.E: Enable Logging export to Google BigQuery and use ACLs and views to scope the data shared with the auditor

explanation: A properly implemented tokenization service substitutes tokens for primary account numbers and confines cardholder data to a tightly controlled flow. Systems outside that flow can analyze transactions using tokens and payment-method attributes without storing or transmitting the card numbers, which reduces PCI DSS assessment scope.

question: You are deploying a highly confidential data-processing workload on Google Cloud. Your company’s compliance framework requires that cryptographic keys used to encrypt data at rest be generated and stored exclusively in a validated Hardware Security Module (HSM). You want to use a fully integrated, Google Cloud-managed service to manage these keys’ lifecycle and use. What should you do?

options.A: Use Customer-Supplied Encryption Keys (CSEK) by providing your on-premises generated key with each API request.
options.B: Import your on-premises HSM key material into a Cloud KMS key with the SOFTWARE protection level.
options.C: Create a new key in Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS) with the HSM protection level.
options.D: Configure Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM) to connect to your on-premises HSM.

explanation: Cloud KMS keys with the HSM protection level are generated, stored, and used for cryptographic operations in Cloud HSM’s validated hardware security modules, while Cloud KMS provides the managed key lifecycle and integration with Google Cloud services.

question: You are deploying a single Cloud SQL for MySQL database that stores business-critical transaction data. You want to make sure the least possible amount of data is lost if a catastrophic failure occurs. Which two features should you implement?

options.A: Sharding
options.B: Read replicas
options.C: Binary logging
options.D: Automated backups
options.E: Semisynchronous replication

explanation: Cloud SQL for MySQL point-in-time recovery requires both automated backups and continuous binary logging. The backup provides the recovery base, and binary logs preserve transaction changes after that backup so the database can be restored to a selected point in time, minimizing data loss.

question:
For this question, refer to the KnightMotives Automotive case study. KnightMotives has deployed its new Dealer Tools on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), and you are supporting performance of the GKE workloads. Some Pods are stateful.

To prevent these Pods from using an unlimited amount of CPU, you configured resource limits on the Deployments. You determined that the Pods were allocated too much CPU and, at times, consume drastically less. You want to optimize resource use while allowing maximum flexibility if load increases. What should you do?

options.A: Configure resource requests per Deployment. Set resource requests slightly above the typical CPU usage observed during monitoring.
options.B: Configure resource requests per Deployment. Ensure the requests are equal to the current limits.
options.C: Enable vertical Pod autoscaling on each Deployment. Ensure the autoscaling mode is set to Auto.
options.D: Enable horizontal Pod autoscaling on each Deployment. Ensure the minimum number of Pods is lower than the currently configured amount in the Deployment.

explanation: GKE Vertical Pod Autoscaling analyzes workload usage over time and automatically adjusts container CPU and memory resource requests and limits. Its Auto mode applies those adjustments as workload requirements change, which rightsizes over-allocated Pods while retaining capacity to adapt to higher usage. Horizontal Pod Autoscaling changes the number of Pod replicas rather than correcting per-Pod CPU allocation. Google Cloud: Vertical Pod autoscaling

question: You are migrating your on-premises solution to Google Cloud in multiple phases. You will use Cloud VPN to keep a connection between your on-premises systems and Google Cloud until the migration is complete. You need to ensure that all on-premises systems remain reachable during this time. How should you arrange your Google Cloud networking?

options.A: Use the same IP range on Google Cloud as you use on-premises
options.B: Use the same IP range on Google Cloud as you use on-premises for your primary IP range and use a secondary range that does not overlap with the range you use on-premises
options.C: Use an IP range on Google Cloud that does not overlap with the range you use on-premises
options.D: Use an IP range on Google Cloud that does not overlap with the range you use on-premises for your primary IP range and use a secondary range with the same IP range as you use on-premises

explanation: Cloud VPN requires non-overlapping Google Cloud VPC and on-premises IP ranges for unambiguous routing. If the same subnet range exists in both places, routes for the on-premises range cannot be used through the VPN (or are ignored with dynamic routing), so traffic for that range stays within the VPC rather than reaching the on-premises systems.

question: You are configuring a new regional environment for your business requirements. You intend to migrate more than 2 TB of data from the us-central1 region to the asia-southeast1 region. The transfer must take place as quickly as possible. If it is interrupted, the operation must continue from where it stopped and copy only new or changed objects. What should you do?

options.A: Use the gcloud storage cp command to copy the objects. Be careful to manage potential naming conflicts to ensure data integrity.
options.B: Utilize Storage Transfer Service (STS) to migrate objects to the destination bucket in the target region. Once the transfer is complete, delete the original source bucket objects.
options.C: Use the gcloud storage rsync --recursive command to replicate the source bucket to a new target bucket in the us-west1 region.
options.D: Leverage Managed Service for Apache Airflow to orchestrate a data pipeline that copies objects from the source bucket to the destination bucket.

explanation: Storage Transfer Service is designed for large Cloud Storage bucket migrations and provides managed performance, reliability, and retry handling. It can resume a paused transfer operation from the point at which it was paused, and its transfers are incremental by default, so later runs transfer only objects that changed after the initial transfer.

question: Mountkirk Games' gaming servers are failing to scale automatically as expected. Last month, they released a new feature that suddenly became very popular. A record number of users are attempting to use the service, but many are receiving 503 errors and experiencing very slow response times. What should they investigate first?

options.A: Verify that the database is online
options.B: Verify that the project quota hasn't been exceeded
options.C: Verify that the new feature code did not introduce any performance bugs
options.D: Verify that the load-testing team is not running their tool against production

explanation: Compute Engine managed instance group autoscaling can fail to add instances when the project lacks quota for required resources, such as CPUs or VM instances. Insufficient capacity leaves the existing servers overloaded during a traffic spike, producing slow responses and HTTP 503 errors.

question: Your organization stores sensitive data in a Cloud Storage bucket. Because of regulatory requirements, the company must be able to rotate the encryption key that protects the bucket’s data. The data will be processed in Managed Service for Apache Spark. You want to follow Google-recommended security practices. What should you do?

options.A: Create a key with Cloud Key Management Service (KMS). Encrypt the data using the encrypt method of Cloud KMS.
options.B: Create a key with Cloud Key Management Service (KMS). Set the encryption key on the bucket to the Cloud KMS key.
options.C: Generate a GPG key pair. Encrypt the data using the GPG key. Upload the encrypted data to the bucket.
options.D: Generate an AES-256 encryption key. Encrypt the data in the bucket using the customer-supplied encryption keys feature.

explanation: Cloud Storage supports customer-managed encryption keys (CMEKs) from Cloud Key Management Service. Configuring a Cloud KMS key as the bucket’s encryption key lets Cloud Storage perform server-side encryption while the organization controls key rotation, permissions, and lifecycle through Cloud KMS.

question:
Dress4Win has asked for your advice on migrating its on-premises MySQL deployment to the cloud.

They want to minimize downtime and performance impact on their on-premises solution during the migration.

Which approach should you recommend?

options.A: Create a dump of the on-premises MySQL master server, and then shut it down, upload it to the cloud environment, and load into a new MySQL cluster.
options.B: Setup a MySQL replica server/slave in the cloud environment, and configure it for asynchronous replication from the MySQL master server on-premises until cutover.
options.C: Create a new MySQL cluster in the cloud, configure applications to begin writing to both on premises and cloud MySQL masters, and destroy the original cluster at cutover.
options.D: Create a dump of the MySQL replica server into the cloud environment, load it into: Google Cloud Datastore, and configure applications to read/write to Cloud Datastore at cutover.

explanation: Asynchronous replication from the on-premises MySQL primary to a cloud replica keeps the cloud copy continuously synchronized while the existing deployment remains online. After replication catches up, applications can be redirected during a brief cutover, minimizing downtime and avoiding the consistency risks of simultaneous writes to separate masters. Google Cloud documents replication from an external MySQL server as a migration approach that achieves minimum downtime.

question: You need to establish a private connection between your Compute Engine instances and your on-premises data center. The connection must provide at least 20 Gbps, and you want to follow Google-recommended practices. How should you configure the connection?

options.A: Create a VPC and connect it to your on-premises data center using Dedicated Interconnect.
options.B: Create a VPC and connect it to your on-premises data center using a single Cloud VPN.
options.C: Create a Cloud Content Delivery Network (Cloud CDN) and connect it to your on-premises data center using Dedicated Interconnect.
options.D: Create a Cloud Content Delivery Network (Cloud CDN) and connect it to your on-premises datacenter using a single Cloud VPN.

explanation: Dedicated Interconnect directly connects an on-premises network to Google’s network and supports capacity using one or more 10-Gbps circuits, so it can meet a 20-Gbps requirement. The connection is attached to a VPC network, which provides connectivity for Compute Engine instances. A single Cloud VPN tunnel does not provide comparable throughput, and Cloud CDN is not a hybrid private-connectivity service.

question: Your company runs a stateless application on a Compute Engine instance. The application is heavily used during normal business hours and lightly used outside those hours. Users report that the application is slow during peak periods. You need to optimize the application's performance. What should you do?

options.A: Create a snapshot of the existing disk. Create an instance template from the snapshot. Create an autoscaled managed instance group from the instance template.
options.B: Create a snapshot of the existing disk. Create a custom image from the snapshot. Create an autoscaled managed instance group from the custom image.
options.C: Create a custom image from the existing disk. Create an instance template from the custom image. Create an autoscaled managed instance group from the instance template.
options.D: Create an instance template from the existing disk. Create a custom image from the instance template. Create an autoscaled managed instance group from the custom image.

explanation: An autoscaled managed instance group adds VM instances as workload demand rises and removes them as demand falls, which suits a stateless application with peak-hour load. Managed instance groups are created from an instance template; creating a custom image from the existing disk allows that template to reproduce the application’s VM configuration consistently.

question:
A company has a Google Cloud project that uses BigQuery for data warehousing. It has a VPN tunnel between its on-premises environment and Google Cloud, configured with Cloud VPN. The security team wants to prevent data exfiltration by malicious insiders, compromised code, and accidental oversharing.

What should the company do?

options.A: Configure Private Google Access for on-premises only.
options.B: Perform the following tasks: 1. Create a service account. 2. Give the BigQuery JobUser role and Storage Reader role to the service account. 3. Remove all other IAM access from the project.
options.C: Configure VPC Service Controls and configure Private Google Access.
options.D: Configure Private Google Access.

explanation: VPC Service Controls establishes a service perimeter around BigQuery and other supported Google-managed services, restricting access and data movement to mitigate exfiltration by insiders, compromised credentials or code, and unintended sharing. Private Google Access enables the on-premises private hosts, connected through Cloud VPN, to reach Google APIs within that protected perimeter.

question:
A small subset of API requests to your microservices-based application takes a very long time. You know that each API request can traverse many services.

You want to identify which service takes the longest in those situations. What should you do?

options.A: Set timeouts on your application so that you can fail requests faster
options.B: Send custom metrics for each of your requests to Cloud Monitoring
options.C: Use Cloud Monitoring to look for insights that show when your API latencies are high
options.D: Instrument your application with Cloud Trace in order to break down the request latencies at each microservice

explanation: Cloud Trace is a distributed tracing system that captures request latency and spans for operations such as RPC calls. Instrumenting each microservice lets a single request be traced across services and its per-service durations compared, revealing the service responsible for the longest portion of the request.

question: You work with a data-warehousing team that performs data analysis. The team must process data from external partners, but that data contains personally identifiable information (PII). You need to process and store the data without storing any of the PIIE data. What should you do?

options.A: Create a Dataflow pipeline to retrieve the data from the external sources. As part of the pipeline, use Sensitive Data Protection (DLP API) to remove any PII data. Store the result in BigQuery.
options.B: Create a Dataflow pipeline to retrieve the data from the external sources. As part of the pipeline, store all non-PII data in BigQuery and store all PII data in a Cloud Storage bucket that has a retention policy set.
options.C: Ask the external partners to upload all data on Cloud Storage. Configure Bucket Lock for the bucket. Create a Dataflow pipeline to read the data from the bucket. As part of the pipeline, use Sensitive Data Protection (DLP API) to remove any PII data. Store the result in BigQuery.
options.D: Ask the external partners to import all data in your BigQuery dataset. Create a dataflow pipeline to copy the data into a new table. As part of the Dataflow bucket, skip all data in columns that have PII data

explanation: Sensitive Data Protection (formerly Cloud DLP) can detect PII and apply de-identification transformations such as masking, replacement, or removal. Applying those transformations in a Dataflow ingestion pipeline before writing to BigQuery ensures that the stored warehouse output contains no PII, while retaining the non-sensitive data for analysis.

question:
A company develops rendering software that users can download from its website. The company has customers worldwide and wants to minimize latency for every customer while following Google-recommended practices.

How should the files be stored?

options.A: Save the files in a multi-region Cloud Storage bucket.
options.B: Save the files in a regional Cloud Storage bucket, one bucket per zone of the region.
options.C: Save the files in multiple regional Cloud Storage buckets, one bucket per zone per region.
options.D: Save the files in multiple multi-region Cloud Storage buckets, one bucket per multi-region.

explanation: Cloud Storage recommends multi-region bucket locations for cross-geography data access and content serving. Storing the downloadable content in a multi-region bucket for each multi-region places it across the major geographic areas, supporting low-latency access for global customers.

question:
Your company has chosen to make a major revision to its API to provide better experiences for its developers. It must keep the old API version available and deployable while allowing new customers and testers to try the new API. It wants to retain the same SSL and DNS records to serve both APIs.

What should it do?

options.A: Configure a new load balancer for the new version of the API
options.B: Reconfigure old clients to use a new endpoint for the new API
options.C: Have the old API forward traffic to the new API based on the path
options.D: Use separate backend pools for each API path behind the load balancer

explanation: A URL map on an HTTPS/Application Load Balancer can route requests by URL path to different backend services while retaining one frontend IP address, DNS name, and SSL configuration. Assigning each API path to its own backend pool enables the old and new API versions to remain independently available and deployable.

question: Your company and one of its partners each own a Google Cloud project in separate organizations. Your company’s project (prj-a) runs in Virtual Private Cloud (vpc-a). The partner’s project (prj-b) runs in vpc-b. Two instances run in vpc-a, and one instance runs in vpc-b. The subnets defined in the two VPCs do not overlap. You need to ensure that every instance can communicate with the others through internal IP addresses while minimizing latency and maximizing throughput. What should you do?

options.A: Set up a network peering between vpc-a and vpc-b.
options.B: Set up a VPN between vpc-a and vpc-b using Cloud VPN.
